rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged deities will deny knowing their worshippers, say they never sought worship, and leave them to face the consequences.
rows.anchor: they had no knowledge that some foolish people used to worship them; they never asked for this worship.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression evokes unleashing a dog on prey; the word used here means to incite.
rows.anchor: some unleashed the dog on the prey. Precisely this style is adopted here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents are treated according to God's established practice stated in al-Zukhruf:36.
rows.anchor: of God mentioned thus in verse 36 of S ūrah al-Zukhruf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lets devils incite the hostile opponents so the truth is conclusively conveyed; their increasing enmity brings them nearer to doom.
rows.anchor: God has let loose devils on them to incite them as much as they can

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to the opening counsel from Gabriel to wait patiently, now as God's direct final warning to the enemies and glad tidings to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: this section of verses began with Gabriel’s advice to the Prophet (sws) to wait and exercise patience. This same topic is now brought up here in another way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The language indicates that the opponents' hostility had reached its limit and the Prophet awaited God's decision.
rows.anchor: these verses were revealed at the time when enmity of these people had reached its ultimate extent

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is counting every moment; when the opponents' appointed time expires, they will receive no further respite.
rows.anchor: Every single moment is being counted by God. Once their time expires, they will not even get a moment’s respite.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafd denotes arriving with honor, like envoys going to a leader or king.
rows.anchor: messengers go to a leader or to the court of a king.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wird means coming to a water spring as thirsty camels do.
rows.anchor: means to come to a spring of water just as thirsty camels do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers the exception severed, thereby denying the alleged deities' claim to intercession.
rows.anchor: They negate the intercession of these alleged deities.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession is an honor God gives only to worthy prophets and witnesses to the truth.
rows.anchor: Only the prophets and witnesses to the truth will have the prerogative to intercede.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercessors act only with God's permission for those specifically permitted; they cannot initiate an appeal on their own.
rows.anchor: They will not be authorized to take the initiative to intercede for someone they do not have permission.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercession remains wholly truthful and cannot turn falsehood into truth before God.
rows.anchor: Their intercession will entirely be based on the truth. It does not behove them to convert falsehood into the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no intercession for polytheists, disbelievers, or people whose professed faith is accompanied by lifelong wrongdoing and disobedience.
rows.anchor: There will be no intercession for those who spent their lives in polytheism and disbelief

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope belongs to believers who did good and repented despite lapses; relying on intercession to persist in sin is baseless wishful thinking.
rows.anchor: only they can hope for intercession who spent their lives on faith, did righteous deeds and sought repentance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam links the claims about divine offspring to Jews, Christians and Arabian idolaters; Arabs called angels God's daughters, Jews Ezra His son, and Christians gave Jesus this status.
rows.anchor: as well as masculine and feminine genders.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting false intercession, the passage rejects the ascription of divine offspring, which grew from hopes of obtaining a license for sin.
rows.anchor: The previous verse refuted the wrong concept of intercession. Now in the succeeding verses, this heinous form of polytheism is refuted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term describes something grave and ominous.
rows.anchor: refers to something very grave and ominous.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from indirect narration to direct address conveys the severity of God's anger, as earlier at 19:71.
rows.anchor: Indirect narration has changed into a direct address. This shift in address from indirect to direct is done to express severity of anger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing partners violates God's peerlessness and sense of honor; even human beings reject dishonor, so God cannot tolerate worship of another.
rows.anchor: God has a great sense of honour for His peerlessness and will never tolerate anything like this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ancient scriptures liken God's honor to a spouse's inability to bear infidelity, underscoring the disgrace of a servant prostrating to another.
rows.anchor: when you cannot bear your wife sleeping with anyone else, how can the honourable God bear His servant prostrating before someone else.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, sun, and moon have an Abrahamic nature that abhors attributing offspring or partners to God, though they cannot act independently of Him.
rows.anchor: the heavens and the earth and the sun and the moon have an Abrahamic nature.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens' and earth's fury is caused by people ascribing children to the Most Merciful.
rows.anchor: Stated in this verse is the reason for the fury and anger of the heavens and the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no children: He requires neither a helper, heir, successor to His work, nor support in old age.
rows.anchor: He neither needs any helper to accomplish His tasks nor any heir to His possessions and assets.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every creature in heaven and earth is God's servant on equal footing; none is His son or daughter.
rows.anchor: Each and every one is His servant equal in status. None shall be His son or daughter there.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete count leaves nothing outside His control or unrecorded; each person appears alone and answers for their own deeds.
rows.anchor: Everyone will be in complete control of God on the Day of Judgement. He would have counted everything

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers receive love and welcome: angels greet them, God sends salutations, and they congratulate each other as a victorious company.
rows.anchor: the angels too will welcome the believers with peace and blessings and salutations shall be conveyed to them from God as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farahi called Maryam the Rahmani surah because the name Rahman is repeated here more than in any other surah; the repetition has thematic purpose.
rows.anchor: Far āhī used to call it the Ra ḥmānī sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Christians' mistaken view made humanity eternally sinful and salvation impossible unless God's son atoned for believers' sins by sacrifice.
rows.anchor: since human beings were eternal sinners and had remained so ever since their inception, hence there was no possibility of their salvation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews presumed their prophetic ancestry secured them from Hell, or that any punishment would last only briefly before mercy forgave them.
rows.anchor: they were the progeny of prophets and the righteous and hence could not be cast into Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabian idolaters denied the reality of Judgment but expected God's angel-daughters to secure them through intercession if it occurred.
rows.anchor: The Idolaters of Arabia worshipped the angels, regarding them to be the daughters of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy does not cancel justice; both reward for truth and warning or punishment for rebellion express mercy.
rows.anchor: His mercy does not negate His justice and His justice is a requisite of His mercy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiving rebels due to lineage, intercession, or attachment to an alleged divine son would be oppression, not mercy.
rows.anchor: If He forgives the unjust and the rebellious because they are descendents of prophets and revered personalities or because someone has interceded for them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment can manifest mercy because wrongdoing harms creatures, while divine limits protect and develop them; criminals are not merely God's personal concern.
rows.anchor: they are for the protection of His creatures and for their development.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's warnings and glad tidings are grounded in the true requirements of God's attribute al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: the warnings and glad tidings found in it are all based on this attribute.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unexpressed pronoun antecedent is the Qur'an, understood from the surah's opening discussion of the prophets' shared message; omission is eloquent and signals its majesty.
rows.anchor: the antecedent can only be the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taysir does not mean making the Qur'an intellectually simple; it means equipping it aptly with everything needed for its purpose of instruction and reminder.
rows.anchor: It means making something appropriate and apt by equipping it with all that is needed for its objective.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawman luddan refers to the Quraysh; luddan is the plural of a term for someone belligerent and stubborn.
rows.anchor: The latter means someone who is belligerent and stubborn.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh's tribal life and illiteracy fostered rigidity and prejudice, leading them to oppose and harass the Prophet with repeated demands.
rows.anchor: because of living in tribal societies and were also very rigid and prejudiced because of being unlettered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the surah's close, the Qur'an is presented as apt and persuasive for conclusive communication in the Prophet's language; he must give glad tidings to the God-fearing and warn the belligerent of worldly and afterlife punishment.
rows.anchor: His only obligation is to give glad tidings of success to those who fear God. As for the belligerent and aggressive among them, he should warn them of punishment in this world and in the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raqz means the sound of someone approaching; prior nations were destroyed and erased, warning that these deniers will likewise be wiped out.
rows.anchor: There are a lot of lessons they can learn from history. Before them many nations were destroyed by God’s punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first major section recounts Moses' rescue as a child, killing of a Copt, move to Madyan and call at Tuwa, mission to Pharaoh, contest with magicians, exodus, sea crossing, and the Samiri calf trial.
rows.anchor: The incident of killing of a Copt at the hands of Moses (sws) is mentioned. Moses (sws) then sets off to Madyan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses' account, the concluding verses address Muhammad and return to the surah's opening theme.
rows.anchor: sūrah ends on the topic with which it began

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must await God's decision patiently; haste gives Satan an opening, as Adam's haste led to his deception, and prayer helps secure patience.
rows.anchor: It was because of hastiness that Adam (sws) was deceived by Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should not pursue the wealthy to bolster his ranks because God provides his preaching's resources and financial needs.
rows.anchor: His preaching has its own resources and God has taken upon Himself to fulfil his financial needs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those demanding punishment should be told that the Prophet's duty was to warn; he too awaits the punishment.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) too is waiting.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening letters are among the isolated letters; a detailed discussion appears under al-Baqarah 2:1.
rows.anchor: under the first verse of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's assumed burden of preaching exceeds what is required of him; the verse begins to clarify his limited responsibility.
rows.anchor: the burden he is bearing as a result is not required of him at all.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's duty is to communicate the Book; he need not force it on people unable to recognize truth and fear God.
rows.anchor: is to communicate this Book to people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing persistent denial and hard hearts made the Prophet worry that his effort was inadequate, but the verse reassures him not to exceed his duty or feel responsible for others' acceptance.
rows.anchor: the verse assures him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhkira means reminder: the Qur'an recalls truths already present in human nature rather than imposing an alien teaching.
rows.anchor: its purpose too is precisely the same.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic reminders draw arguments from the inner and outer worlds, reason, familiar history, and teachings to which the audience claims descent.
rows.anchor: which these addressees claimed to be a progeny and followers of.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of 'fear' is omitted; parallel Qur'anic wording supplies 'their Lord unseen,' as in al-Baqarah 2:2.
rows.anchor: The grammatical object of the verb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety is natural where human nature remains sound; Qur'anic reminders awaken such people, while those who have corrupted their nature remain unmoved.
rows.anchor: As for those who pervert their natures

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who demand sensory proof understand only force, but God values belief acknowledged through intellect rather than observation.
rows.anchor: before God, only that belief has weight

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Qur'an is a reminder, the Prophet's task is to remind rather than coerce; whether people benefit is their responsibility, so their failure should not distress him.
rows.anchor: the responsibility of the people and not his.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanzil means gradual, thorough revelation; the Qur'an came in episodes so people could not claim they failed to understand it.
rows.anchor: reveal something in a thorough and gradual manner.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the creator of earth and lofty skies magnifies the Qur'an's source: it is the Creator's directive, not a baseless claim or petition.
rows.anchor: the majesty of the Being Who revealed it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should present the Book as the Creator's word without either consoling or pressuring people; acceptance benefits them, while rejection brings consequences to them.
rows.anchor: nor force or pressurize them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the Qur'an's reminder to the account of its honored, protected pages in Sūrah ʿAbas.
rows.anchor: for example in Sūrah ‘Abas, it is stated:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy requires guidance as well as material provision; God gives intellect and intuition and then the Qur'an, as the opening of al-Rahman also indicates.
rows.anchor: blessed them with intellect and intuition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God remains sovereign over the created world and communicates His directives through the Qur'an; those who knowingly reject it face accountability.
rows.anchor: He did not become aloof after creating the world; He is in fact running its affairs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in and below the heavens and earth lies within God's control, leaving no escape or refuge besides Him and uprooting polytheism.
rows.anchor: there is no part of this universe that is beyond God’s control and jurisdiction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eloquent Arabic suppresses the parallel clause: whether speech is open or secret, God knows what is hidden and still more hidden.
rows.anchor: parallel portion of the verse are suppressed because of concomitant indications.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is reassured that God hears his pleadings in any state in which he voices them.
rows.anchor: all his pleadings to God are heard by Him in whatever state he utters them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is to be worshipped; since His knowledge encompasses everything, no other deity is needed.
rows.anchor: When this is the case, why should anyone other than Him be made a deity? When He hears and knows everything, He alone is sufficient.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final section resumes the introductory theme and addresses the Prophet: opponents who lead others astray carry both their own sins and those of their followers.
rows.anchor: will not only bear their own burden of sins on the Day of Judgement but also of those who were led astray by them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should recite the comprehensive warning to all; willing hearers benefit, evasive people are left alone, and he is not accountable for them.
rows.anchor: he who evades it should be left alone by him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should endure sarcastic remarks patiently and cling to prayer to attain patience; those demanding punishment should be directed to local history, and he should not pursue the wealthy to make them believe.
rows.anchor: patient on their sarcastic remarks
